referents.why: him (auton) is the object of Pilate's questioning, Jesus
how many (poson) is an interrogative quantity over the charges; no candidate is what it refers to
against you (sou) in the charges is second person singular, addressed to Jesus in Pilate's speech
implied you in Have you no answer? is Jesus, addressee of Pilate's question
they bring the charges: the chief priests of Mrk.15.3 are the accusers, but no candidate for them is offered; the nearest plural, elders and scribes (c8), are not the accusers

links.why: participle saying is nested in the main verb of asking
self link; a clause does not follow itself
the question is what the saying participle introduces; recorded as content (R1), not nesting
saying introduces Have you no answer? (R1)
the second sentence, Look how many charges, is also what is said in the same speech (R1)
two sentences of one speech with no connective between them, not one nested in the other

groups.why: Pilate's speech to Jesus: frame is the asking, parts are the two sentences said; the saying participle cl1 is not itself said, so removed as part; addressee Jesus added

none_fit.what: two sentences of one speech set side by side without a connective; no link type for juxtaposed sentences, the turn carries them

cant_tell.what: referent of cl3s (the accusers, they bring charges)
cant_tell.why: the chief priests of Mrk.15.3 are the plausible accusers but are not among the candidates offered for this verse
